text: We evaluated a contrastive-consistency probe on the strong model's hidden states, reading from probe layer 18, on the sciq testbed across 16 seeds. The measured performance gap recovered (PGR) was 0.13 with a standard error of 0.12. Because the standard error is nearly as large as the point estimate itself, the data are compatible with a PGR at or near zero, and we cannot treat this as evidence that the probe recovers a meaningful share of the gap. No baseline PGR was supplied in this experiment, so there is no reference point against which to assess whether the probe outperforms an alternative weak-to-strong method; any claim of improvement would be unsupported. The 16-seed sample does, however, give a reasonably well-characterized estimate of the spread, and the breadth of that spread is the main finding: the effect, if present, is small relative to seed-to-seed variation. Further seeds or a specified baseline would be needed to draw a directional conclusion.
